stem:
The function $\mathrm{f}$ is defined by
$$\mathrm{f}(x) = 4 - 2|x + 1|, \quad x \in \mathbb{R}.$$

parts.label: a
parts.text: Sketch $y = \mathrm{f}(x)$ for all real $x$. Your sketch must display the coordinates of the vertex of the graph and of all three points where the graph intersects the coordinate axes. (2)

mark_scheme.for: An inverted V shape made of two straight line segments, with its single highest point at $(-1, 4)$, in the second quadrant.
mark_scheme.notes: The vertex coordinates may be written on the sketch or stated in the text. Curved arms, or an upright V, score B0.

mark_scheme.for: Shows the $x$-axis crossings at $(-3, 0)$ and $(1, 0)$ and the $y$-axis crossing at $(0, 2)$, all on a graph of the correct shape.
mark_scheme.notes: Accept $-3$, $1$ and $2$ marked on the correct axes. All three are needed for this mark.

solution.working: $\mathrm{f}(x) = -2|x+1| + 4$: the graph of $y = |x|$ is shifted 1 unit left, stretched by scale factor 2 parallel to the $y$-axis, reflected in the $x$-axis and then shifted 4 units up. It is an inverted V with vertex where $x + 1 = 0$, so at $(-1, 4)$.
Crosses the $x$-axis where $2|x+1| = 4$, so $|x + 1| = 2$, giving $x = 1$ or $x = -3$. At $x = 0$: $\mathrm{f}(0) = 4 - 2(1) = 2$. So the intercepts are $(-3, 0)$, $(1, 0)$ and $(0, 2)$.

hints: The vertex is where the expression inside the modulus is zero. Think about which way the minus sign in front of $2|x+1|$ turns the V.
To find where the graph meets the $x$-axis, solve $|x + 1| = 2$. For the $y$-intercept, substitute $x = 0$.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The graph of $y = \mathrm{f}(x)$ is transformed in two separate ways. Write down the coordinates of the vertex of the graph of
(i) $y = \mathrm{f}(x - 5)$,
(ii) $y = 3\mathrm{f}\left(\tfrac{1}{2}x\right)$. (2)

mark_scheme.notes: Both coordinates needed. Also accept $x = 4$, $y = 4$ stated clearly.

solution.working: (i) $\mathrm{f}(x-5)$ is a translation of 5 units in the positive $x$-direction, so the vertex $(-1, 4)$ moves to $(-1 + 5, 4) = (4, 4)$.

(ii) $\mathrm{f}\left(\tfrac12 x\right)$ is a stretch by scale factor 2 parallel to the $x$-axis, and the factor 3 is a stretch by scale factor 3 parallel to the $y$-axis. So $(-1, 4)$ goes to $(2 \times (-1),\ 3 \times 4) = (-2, 12)$. Check: $\tfrac12(-2) + 1 = 0$ and $3(4 - 0) = 12$.

hints: Start from the vertex $(-1, 4)$ you found in part (a) and work out what each transformation does to it.
Replacing $x$ by $x - 5$ or by $\tfrac12 x$ changes only the $x$-coordinate. Multiplying the whole function by 3 changes only the $y$-coordinate.

pitfalls.text: The $+1$ inside $|x + 1|$ moves the graph 1 unit to the left, so the vertex is at $x = -1$. If you put it at $x = 1$, every coordinate on your sketch is wrong and both B marks are lost. This is a common slip.

The $-2$ in front of the modulus turns the graph upside down, so it is an inverted V with a sharp point at the top. The arms are straight lines. A lot of students draw an upright V, or round off the vertex into a curve, and that loses the first B1.

Students often leave out the $y$-intercept or get it wrong, e.g. writing $(0, 4)$ by reading off the constant term. In fact $\mathrm{f}(0) = 4 - 2 = 2$. If you omit $(0, 2)$ or either of $(-3, 0)$ and $(1, 0)$, you lose the second B1.
$\mathrm{f}(x - 5)$ moves the graph 5 units to the right, not the left. A common mistake is to give $(-6, 4)$, which loses the first B1.
In $\mathrm{f}\left(\tfrac12 x\right)$ the $x$-coordinates are multiplied by 2, not by $\tfrac12$. Writing $\left(-\tfrac12, 12\right)$ is a common error and loses the second B1.

In (ii) the vertex moves in both directions. If you apply only the horizontal stretch and give $(-2, 4)$, forgetting that the factor 3 triples the $y$-coordinate to 12, you lose the second B1. Many students make this slip.

parts.label: a
parts.working_summary: Inverted V shape with vertex (-1,4). f(0)=2. 4-2|x+1|=0 gives x=1 or x=-3.

parts.label: b(i)
parts.working_summary: Translation by 5 in the positive x-direction: (-1,4) goes to (4,4).

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.working_summary: Horizontal stretch scale factor 2 and vertical stretch scale factor 3: (-1,4) goes to (-2,12).
